context: A Playwright spec carrying three distinct defects: eight fixed sleeps, styling-coupled selectors, and one mega-test. Predicted baseline failure: the agent removes the obvious sleeps and swaps some selectors, but keeps at least one `waitForTimeout` around the payment step where a sleep feels safest, and reaches for `page.waitForSelector` as the replacement rather than an auto-waiting assertion - which re-introduces an explicit wait the framework already performs. It is also likely to keep the synchronous `isVisible()` / `textContent()` checks, which read state once and do not retry, so the flake survives the rewrite.

checklist.name: No fixed-duration waits remain
checklist.description: The delivered spec contains no `waitForTimeout`, no `setTimeout`-based sleep, and no other call that pauses for a hard-coded number of milliseconds. Any single surviving fixed sleep scores zero for this criterion, whatever the rest of the rewrite looks like - the flake is caused by timing assumptions and one remaining sleep preserves it.

checklist.name: Waiting is done by retrying assertions, not explicit wait calls
checklist.description: Readiness is expressed as `await expect(locator).toBeVisible()` / `.toHaveText()` / `.toHaveCount()` and similar, which retry until the timeout. Replacing sleeps with `page.waitForSelector` / `waitForLoadState` / `waitForFunction` as the primary mechanism scores at most half: it removes the fixed duration but still hand-rolls waiting the assertion performs. Keeping `expect(await page.isVisible(...)).toBe(true)` or `expect(await page.textContent(...)).toBe(...)` scores zero for that assertion's share, because those evaluate once and cannot retry.

checklist.name: Selectors survive a CSS refactor
checklist.description: Element lookups use role, label, text, or an explicit test id rather than class names, `nth-child` positions, or XPath. A spec still selecting on `.btn--primary`, `.product-card`, `.nav-links > li:nth-child(2)` or equivalent scores zero here. Using a stable `data-testid` counts as passing even though it is not role-based.

checklist.name: One test per flow
checklist.description: The single mega-test is split so a failure names the flow. At least three separate `test(...)` blocks covering sign-in, cart, and checkout. A single test with comments or `test.step` markers scores at most half - a mid-test failure still does not name the flow in the report.

checklist.name: Shared setup is factored, not copy-pasted
checklist.description: Sign-in or navigation needed by more than one test is reached through a helper, fixture, `beforeEach`, or page-object method rather than the same block pasted into each test.

checklist.name: login.spec.ts left unchanged
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify tests/login.spec.ts. It is stated to be stable and out of scope; editing it scores zero here.

checklist.name: Assertions still cover the original checkpoints
checklist.description: The rewrite still asserts the welcome state after sign-in, a cart count of 1, and the order confirmation. Dropping a checkpoint while cleaning up scores zero for this criterion - the suite must not get more reliable by testing less.
